cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: What Aren’t You Saying?
cards.instruction: Find out what someone is holding back by treating every careful answer as incomplete.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. You called my audition interesting. What came after that in your head? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're my sister. I'm trying to be encouraging.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Then give me the encouraging half and the half you swallowed.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your singing was better than your dancing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Better by how much? Are we buying dance lessons or shoes that don't move?

mechanism: A directs audition feedback and promises not to argue so B will complete increasingly careful answers rather than protect A feelings.
confusable: Unlike merely seeking praise or an evaluation, A treats each softened answer as concealing another part; borrowed authority modifies the feedback conditions to keep B talking.
comparison: Sibling artistic feedback differs from a colleague withholding names in meeting minutes.
seedUse: Use D102-a interesting/sister/encouraging/singing-versus-dancing and S02-b adapting how feedback is delivered.
